sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the two levels of "greatness" (Gadol) and "holiness" (Kedushah) in the Midrash, and how drawing down the higher level of "My greatness" requires a higher form of service, specifically the service of teshuvah.

translations.translation: Now, the matter of "Can I be like you?" etc. in the aforementioned Midrash comes in continuation of what was stated there previously on the verse,
"And you shall be only above, 'Can I be like you?'... My greatness is above your greatness."
And according to what is stated in Likkutei Torah regarding the matter of "My holiness is above your holiness,"
that it is within the ability of Yisrael to draw down also the aspect of "My holiness" which is above "your holiness," except that the drawing down of this holiness is through a more elevated service
(the service of teshuvah which is above the service of Torah and mitzvos),
it must be said,
that similarly, this is also the case regarding the two levels of greatness
("My greatness" and "your greatness"),
that it is within the ability of Yisrael to draw down also the aspect of "My greatness,"
except that for this, a more elevated service is needed.
And to add,
that holiness is above greatness.
For greatness is the matter of expansion and revelation
[therefore, Chessed is called "Gedulah" (Greatness).
And also according to the explanation that greatness is above the attribute of Chessed,
the matter of greatness is Chessed
(expansion),
except that it is above the attribute of Chessed,
and the expansion that comes from greatness is without limit].
And holiness
(from the term holiness and separation)
is the Essence (Atzmus)
that is separate from the matter of expansion and revelation.
And based on this, it can be said,
that also the drawing down of the aspect of "My greatness" which is above "your greatness" is through the service of the tzaddikim
[except that within the service of the tzaddikim themselves, it is a more elevated service],
and that specifically the service of teshuvah is needed for the drawing down of the aspect of "My holiness."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the verse "The humble will add joy in Hashem" as referring to the drawing down of "My greatness" through the service of the humble tzaddikim, and "the destitute of men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel" as the drawing down of "My holiness" through baalei teshuvah.

translations.translation: And this can be explained according to what is stated,
"The humble will add joy in Hashem, and the destitute of men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel,"
and it is explained in Likkutei Torah
that "the humble will add joy in Hashem" refers to the service of the tzaddikim,
that through their humility and self-nullification they add joy in the Name Havayah,
and through this the revelation of Havayah is drawn down below,
and "the destitute of men" are the baalei teshuvah
[for Torah and mitzvos are called "Adam" (man),
and therefore baalei teshuvah are called "destitute of men" because they are destitute of the aspect of "Adam" of Torah and mitzvos],
who attain the aspect of "the Holy One of Israel,"
which is holy and separate from the aspect of Yisrael above,
above Havayah.
And it can be said,
that the addition of joy in Havayah, through which there is an addition in His drawing down and revelation, is the drawing down of the aspect of "My greatness" which is above "your greatness."
For the greatness
(the expansion)
of Havayah
as it is in His own essence,
is a greatness that relates to worlds and creations,
"your greatness,"
except that there is a limit to His expansion and revelation.
And the matter of "they will add... in Havayah" is that the greatness of the Ein Sof, which is above relation to worlds, is drawn into Him,
"My greatness,"
and through this there is also an addition in the expansion and revelation of Havayah.
For this drawing down is through the service of the tzaddikim,
the humble ones.
And the matter of "and the destitute of men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel" is
the drawing down of the aspect of "My holiness"
(which is above "your holiness")
through teshuvah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse "Who would give you as a brother to me" and the Midrashic interpretation that we ask G-d to be like Yosef to Binyamin, not like Yosef to his other brothers, because the latter involved prior suffering, whereas we seek mercy without afflictions.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by first prefacing
what is stated,
"Who would give you as a brother to me, nursing from my mother's breasts,"
and Rashi explained,
"Who would give you as a brother to me,"
that You should come to comfort me in the manner that Yosef did to his brothers, who repaid him with evil, and it is stated about him,
"And he comforted them."
And in the Midrash
it is stated,
"Which brother? ... You must say, like Yosef to Binyamin."
And the Tzemach Tzedek explains,
that the reason for this, that we ask from the Holy One, blessed be He,
(according to the explanation of the Midrash)
that He should be to us like Yosef to Binyamin and not like Yosef to his brothers,
[even though Yosef's conduct toward his brothers is a greater wonder, for although they did not treat him properly, he nevertheless bestowed great good upon them],
is,
that Yosef's conduct toward his brothers was that initially Yosef caused his brothers distress,
in order
that through this the sin of selling him would be atoned for them
(and only afterwards did he bestow good upon them),
and since we ask,
"Forgive in Your abundant mercies, but not through afflictions,"
therefore we say that the Holy One, blessed be He, should be to us like Yosef to Binyamin.
And it needs to be understood,
behold, the request "Who would give you as a brother to me" is that although our conduct was not proper, nevertheless the Holy One, blessed be He, should be to us as a brother,
and how does the example of "like Yosef to Binyamin" apply to this?
